entities.summary: Harpocration of Argos was an Ancient Greek Middle Platonist philosopher who lived in the second half of the 2nd century CE. He was born in Argos, a city in ancient Greece, and later studied in Athens under the tutelage of prominent philosophers such as Crispianus and Antiochus. Harpocration's philosophical views were heavily influenced by the teachings of Plato, and he became known for his distinctive interpretation of the Platonic ideal of the philosopher-king. Harpocration's writings on the nature of the soul and the ideal state of society were widely read and debated among the intellectual elite of the ancient world. He was particularly known for his critique of the Stoic school and his advocacy for a more nuanced understanding of the human condition. Harpocration's ideas had a lasting impact on Western philosophy, influencing thinkers such as Plotinus and Iamblichus. Despite the passage of time, Harpocration's philosophical legacy continues to be studied and debated by scholars today.
